text:
Philadelphia played the better game and still lost it in the shootout, the kind of result the chance data says was a coin flip tilted the wrong way. PHI generated 3.13 expected goals to SEA's 2.87 and won 55 percent of simulated replays, with the gap coming from the first two periods, when PHI out-chanced SEA 2.13 to 1.10. SEA led 2-0 anyway. Bobby McMann scored on the power play in the first period, and Ville Ottavainen added a snap shot in the second that carried just a 6 percent chance of going in.

The comeback came fast. Christian Dvorak scored at 6:07 of the third, and Trevor Zegras tied it 73 seconds later on a 20 percent look, with Oliver Bonk, Travis Sanheim and Owen Tippett all in the buildup. Sanheim then had the best chance of the night, a 36 percent look in the third that Philipp Grubauer stopped. Grubauer saved 1.13 goals more than the shots he faced deserved, and he was the reason SEA reached overtime still level.

Overtime belonged to SEA, which out-chanced PHI 0.86 to 0.00 in expected goals. The shootout stayed scoreless until Matty Beniers beat Dan Vladar in the first round and Matvei Michkov answered in the second. Nobody scored in rounds three and four, and McMann ended it in round five. Zegras, who took five shots on goal, missed in the first round of the shootout.
